en.name: iNewsBoard
en.short_description: Headlines from BBC News, NPR and The Guardian, sorted by topic.
en.subtitle: Publisher feeds, by topic
en.description:
NewsBoard is a reader for news that other people report. It fetches 23 public news feeds from BBC News, BBC Sport, NPR and The Guardian, and shows you what those newsrooms published — their headline, their summary, their byline where they gave one, and the time they published it. NewsBoard writes none of it and changes none of it.

WHERE EVERY STORY COMES FROM
Every article carries the name of the publisher whose feed it arrived in, and opening one gives you a "Read at BBC News" button that takes you to that publisher's own page in your browser. Profile lists all four publishers with a link to each of their sites. If a feed does not supply something — a picture, a byline, a summary — that space is left empty rather than filled in.

BY TOPIC
Technology, business, science, health, politics, sport, entertainment, environment and world, plus a For You view of everything and a Trending view. Trending here means one thing only: the same story is being carried by more than one of the publishers. There is no popularity score, no view count and no ranking, because nothing in the app measures any of those.

READ LATER, FOLLOW, SEARCH
Save any article to read later; saved articles stay on your device. Follow a topic or a hashtag and the Following tab collects matching stories. Search runs across the headlines, summaries, publishers and tags of everything that has loaded.

OFFLINE, HONESTLY
The last set of stories NewsBoard successfully downloaded is kept on the device. With no connection it shows that set and says "Offline · showing stories saved 2h ago" above it, so you always know how old what you are reading is. With nothing downloaded yet it tells you the fetch failed and offers a retry, instead of showing you an empty page that looks like a quiet news day.

WHAT IT DOES NOT DO
No account, no sign-in. No advertising. No subscription and no in-app purchase — there is no paid tier and nothing is held back. Nothing in NewsBoard is generated: no AI summaries, no rewritten headlines. There is no push notification. Market quotes are not available: opening a stock symbol says so rather than showing a made-up price.

review_information.notes:
2. DEVICES AND OS VERSIONS TESTED
Automated tests run on every build: iPhone 17 Pro Max and iPad Pro 13-inch simulators on iOS 26, and a Pixel Android emulator on API 34.
Each release is also installed and launched on those targets, so a
build that cannot start never ships.

3. WHAT THIS APP DOES, AND FOR WHOM
NewsBoard is a reader for news that other people report. It fetches 23 public news feeds from BBC News, BBC Sport, NPR and The Guardian, and shows you what those newsrooms published — their headline, their summary, their byline where they gave one, and the time they published it. NewsBoard writes none of it and changes none of it.

Intended audience:
Publisher feeds, by topic

4. SETTING UP AND REACHING THE MAIN FEATURES
No account and no login are required. Every feature is reachable from the first screen after launch.

5. EXTERNAL SERVICES USED
- HTTPS requests to the app's own endpoints

6. REGIONAL DIFFERENCES
The app ships 12 languages (Arabic, Chinese (Simplified), English, French, German, Hindi, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish). Features are identical in every region.

7. REGULATED INDUSTRY OR THIRD-PARTY MATERIAL

The app is not in a regulated industry and carries no licensed third-party material. All content, artwork and copy are the developer's own.


ACCOUNT DELETION
The app creates no account, so there is nothing to delete.

_was_blocked_resolved.note: Real publisher RSS feeds (BBC, NPR, Guardian) replaced the invented articles on 2026-09-15; seed_articles.dart deleted. A human must still confirm those publishers' syndication terms permit a commercial listing.

previous.feed_licensing: A human has to confirm the app may redistribute these publishers' feeds before it is submitted. The feeds are the publishers' own public RSS, the app shows only the headline, the publisher's summary and a link back, and every item is attributed by name — but BBC and NPR both distinguish personal from business use in their syndication terms, and this is an App Store listing by a company.
previous.evidence: mobile/lib/core/data/feed_sources.dart lists 23 feeds across feeds.bbci.co.uk, feeds.npr.org and theguardian.com. mobile/lib/core/data/rss_parser.dart:105-119 keeps the publisher's own title, link, summary, author and date and derives nothing. mobile/lib/features/article/article_screen.dart renders a "Read at <publisher>" button that opens the publisher's page.
previous.to_unblock: Get written confirmation for each publisher, or swap the list in feed_sources.dart for feeds whose terms already permit this use. The list is the only place feeds are declared; the fetcher, the Profile credits and the tests all read it.

Both numbers exclude the ~60 widgets every Flutter app uses — Column, Text,
Padding and so on. Including them makes any two Flutter apps look 97% alike,
which is a property of the framework rather than of these apps.

The store copy is distinct on the same basis: no two of the 43 share more
than 22% of their description vocabulary.
